newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia peso gains as banks sell greenbacks.
newsitem.headline: Colombia peso gains as banks sell greenbacks.

text.p: Colombia's peso gained 1.65 to 1,072.85 against the dollar in lethargic trading marked by banks swapping greenbacks for pesos to pay first instalments on tax bills.
Interbank traders said the dollar supply was not matched by demand from industry, which prefered to remain on the sidelines to see if the dollar rate would drop further.
"The market was very quiet at the start of trading and then banks came out to change dollars for pesos," one Bogota dealer said.
Dealers reported 263 operations worth a total $112 million, below the daily average of about $180 million. The peso opened at 1,074.25 hit an intraday high of 1,072 and sank to a low of 1,075.2.
